overview: This Senate resolution supports naming May 2025 National Foster Care Month and May 31, 2025, National Foster Parent Appreciation Day. It notes that roughly 368,000 children live in foster care, that many wait years for a permanent home, and that thousands age out each year without a family to rely on. It encourages Congress to adopt policies that help these children, praises foster parents, social workers and former foster youth, and calls for work to prevent family breakups, reunite families when safe, promote adoption when reunification isn't possible, and help young people who age out. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 22, 2025.
for: Supporters say it draws attention to the challenges children in foster care face and honors the foster parents and caseworkers who support them.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it encourages better policies but does not change any law or provide any funding for foster care.
